categories.main_business_segments: Lattice Semiconductor operates primarily in the development and sale of low power, small form factor Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and related solutions. The company organizes its business around three main end markets: Communications and Computing, Industrial and Automotive, and Consumer. It also generates revenue from intellectual property (IP) licensing and services, including standard IP licensing, IP core licensing, patent monetization, and design services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Lattice is a fabless semiconductor company, focusing on proprietary low-power FPGA architectures and platforms such as Certus, ECP, Mach, iCE, and CrossLink device families. The company leverages advanced process technologies (e.g., 28nm FD-SOI, 130nm to 40nm CMOS) through partnerships with foundries like Samsung, UMC, TSMC, and Epson. Assembly and testing are outsourced to leading OSATs, primarily ASE and Amkor, while Lattice invests heavily in R&D for new products, advanced packaging, software tools, and system-level solution stacks.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Lattice serves a global customer base primarily consisting of OEMs in the Communications and Computing (e.g., servers, 5G infrastructure), Industrial and Automotive (e.g., IoT, factory automation, ADAS), and Consumer (e.g., smart home, wearables, AR/VR) sectors. The company also licenses IP to customers integrating Lattice technology into their own ASICs or products, and participates in standards consortia such as HDMI and MHL.
categories.geographic_coverage: Lattice operates globally, with the majority of its revenue (about 75%) coming from Asia, followed by the Americas (16%) and Europe (10%). The company has R&D and operational sites in the US (Oregon, California), Canada, China, and the Philippines, and maintains a network of sales offices and distributors worldwide.
categories.supply_chain_position: Lattice is a fabless, downstream semiconductor provider, focusing on product design, development, and marketing, while outsourcing wafer fabrication, assembly, and testing to third-party foundries and OSATs. The company sits at the downstream end of the supply chain, delivering finished programmable logic devices and solutions to OEMs and distributors.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Lattice's strategic focus is on expanding its leadership in low-power, small form factor FPGAs and accelerating new product introductions for high-growth applications such as Edge AI, 5G infrastructure, platform security, and factory automation. The company invests significantly in R&D for proprietary products, advanced packaging, software development tools, soft IP cores, and integrated hardware/software solution stacks. Recent acquisitions, such as Mirametrix, enhance its AI and computer vision capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: Lattice generates revenue primarily through the sale of silicon-based FPGA products via distributors and direct sales to OEMs, with additional revenue from IP licensing, royalties (e.g., HDMI, MHL), patent sales, and design services. The majority of revenue (over 87%) comes from product sales through distributors, with the remainder from direct sales and licensing/services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Lattice competes with other FPGA vendors (such as Xilinx/AMD, Intel/Altera, and Microchip), as well as suppliers of ASICs, ASSPs, and microcontrollers. The company differentiates itself as the leader in low-power, small form factor FPGAs, targeting applications where power efficiency, size, and flexibility are critical. Lattice is smaller than the largest FPGA competitors but focuses on niche, high-growth segments.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal 2021, Lattice reported revenue of $515 million, up 26% from the prior year, with a gross margin of 62.4% and net income of $95.9 million. The company has demonstrated strong growth, particularly in Industrial & Automotive and Communications & Computing segments, and maintains a healthy balance sheet with $131.6 million in cash and manageable long-term debt.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Lattice emphasizes its leadership in low-power, small form factor, and easy-to-use FPGAs, enabling customers to accelerate time-to-market, reduce power consumption, and integrate advanced features in compact designs. Its flexible, reprogrammable devices, robust software ecosystem, and integrated solution stacks (e.g., sensAI, mVision, Sentry) provide unique value for applications in Edge AI, security, and embedded vision, setting Lattice apart from larger, general-purpose FPGA competitors.
